questions.title: GATE CSE 1994 | Question: 1.2
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $A$ and $B$ be real symmetric matrices of size $n \times n$. Then which one of the following is true?

  1. $AA'=I$
  2. $A=A^{-1}$
  3. $AB=BA$
  4. $(AB)'=BA$

review.independentCheck: For symmetric A and B, (AB)'=B'A'=BA.
review.notes: For symmetric A and B, (AB)'=B'A'=BA.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1994 | Question: 1.4, ISRO2017-2
questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $A$ and $B$ be any two arbitrary events, then, which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. $P (A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$
  2. $P (A \cup B) = P(A)+P(B)$
  3. $P (A \mid B) = P(A \cap B)P(B)$
  4. $P (A \cup B) \leq P(A) + P(B)$

review.independentCheck: Inclusion-exclusion gives the union bound P(A union B)<=P(A)+P(B).
review.notes: Inclusion-exclusion gives the union bound P(A union B)<=P(A)+P(B).

questions.title: GATE CSE 1994 | Question: 1.10
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Some group $(G, o)$ is known to be abelian. Then, which one of the following is true for $G$?

  1. $g=g^{-1} \text{ for every } g \in G$

  2. $g=g^2 \text{ for every }g  \in G$

  3. $(goh)^2 = g^2oh^2 \text{ for every } g, h \in G$

  4. $G$ is of finite order

review.independentCheck: In an abelian group, commute the middle factors to obtain (g o h)^2=g^2 o h^2.
review.notes: In an abelian group, commute the middle factors to obtain (g o h)^2=g^2 o h^2.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1993 | Question: 8.1
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Consider a simple connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $n$ edges $(n > 2)$. Then, which of the following statements are true?

  1. $G$ has no cycles
  2. The graph obtained by removing any edge from $G$ is not connected
  3. $G$ has at least one cycle
  4. The graph obtained by removing any two edges from $G$ is not connected
  5. None of the above

review.independentCheck: A connected graph with m=n has cycle rank one; it is unicyclic, so C and D hold.
review.notes: A connected graph with m=n has cycle rank one; it is unicyclic, so C and D hold.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

  3. logically equivalent to $p \vee q$

  4. a contradiction

  5. none of the above

questions.title: GATE CSE 1993 | Question: 8.3
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let $S$ be an infinite set and $S_1 \dots , S_n$ be sets such that $S_1 \cup S_2 \cup \dots \cup S_n = S$. Then

  1. at least one of the sets $S_i$ is a finite set
  2. not more than one of the sets $S_i$ can be finite
  3. at least one of the sets $S_i$ is an infinite
  4. not more than one of the sets $S_i$ can be infinite
  5. None of the above

review.independentCheck: A finite union of finite sets is finite, so a finite cover of an infinite set has an infinite member.
review.notes: A finite union of finite sets is finite, so a finite cover of an infinite set has an infinite member.
review.answerKeySource: Existing UID answer record cross-checked against the displayed question/options and independent derivation; no answer key changed.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1993 | Question: 8.4
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Let A be a finite set of size n. The number of elements in the power set of $A\times A$ is:

  1. $2^{2^n}$
  2. $2^{n^2}$
  3. $\left(2^n\right)^2$
  4. $\left(2^2\right)^n$
  5. None of the above

review.independentCheck: A cross A has n^2 ordered pairs, so its powerset has 2^(n^2) members.
review.notes: A cross A has n^2 ordered pairs, so its powerset has 2^(n^2) members.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1993 | Question: 8.5
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
The less-than relation, $<$, on reals is

  1. a partial ordering since it is asymmetric and reflexive
  2. a partial ordering since it is antisymmetric and reflexive
  3. not a partial ordering because it is not asymmetric and not reflexive
  4. not a partial ordering because it is not antisymmetric and reflexive
  5. None of the above

review.independentCheck: Less-than is asymmetric and irreflexive; option C falsely denies asymmetry, so E is the only valid choice.
review.notes: Less-than is asymmetric and irreflexive; option C falsely denies asymmetry, so E is the only valid choice.

questions.title: GATE CSE 1992 | Question: 92,xv
questions.subject: Discrete Mathematics
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following predicate calculus statements is/are valid?

  1. $(\forall (x)) P(x) \vee (\forall(x))Q(x) \implies (\forall (x)) (P(x) \vee Q(x))$
  2. $(\exists (x)) P(x) \wedge (\exists (x))Q(x) \implies (\exists (x)) (P(x) \wedge Q(x))$
  3. $(\forall (x)) (P(x) \vee Q(x)) \implies (\forall (x)) P(x) \vee (\forall (x)) Q(x)$
  4. $(\exists (x)) (P(x) \vee Q(x)) \implies \sim (\forall (x)) P(x) \vee (\exists (x)) Q(x)$

review.independentCheck: Only universal-disjunction distribution in option A is valid; counterexamples refute B-D.
review.notes: Only universal-disjunction distribution in option A is valid; counterexamples refute B-D.

questions.questionHtml:
The number of rooted binary trees with $n$ nodes is,

  2. Equal to the number of ways of arranging $n$ out of $2 n$ distinct elements.
  3. Equal to $\frac{1}{(n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}$.
  4. Equal to $n!$.

review.independentCheck: Rooted ordered binary-tree shapes and parenthesizations of n+1 matrices are both counted by Catalan C_n.
